hook_text: Two carpets, both 12 tiles. One needs a longer border. How?
clip_script: Thohoyandou, planning a reading corner on grid paper. Each square is one carpet tile. A 5 by 3 rectangle: 3 rows of 5, 15 tiles. That is 15 square units. An L shape around the bookshelf: 8 plus 4, 12 tiles. A triangle: 6 whole squares and 4 halves. Two halves make one, so 8 square units. Now 4 by 3 and 6 by 2: both 12 tiles, same area. But walk around them: 14 units and 16 units. Area counts the inside; perimeter goes around.
visual_style: Carpet tiles dropping onto a grid one row at a time, then half tiles pairing up to make wholes.
mood: Cosy and clever, like designing a favourite reading spot.
pacing: Count the rectangle, the L, the halves, then the same-area twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and design your own 12-tile carpet on grid paper.
